c3.evidence: No fee to use the database or to apply for utility rebates. Note: rebates require purchasing qualifying equipment — discounts on spending, not income.

s1.note: Varies by utility and state — enter your zip code; nearly all rebates require being a customer of the participating utility and buying qualifying efficient equipment.

s2.note: This is a directory, not a single $1,000 offer — your actual rebate depends entirely on your utility; every rebate requires spending money on equipment first.

s3.note: Instant or 4-8 weeks post-purchase depending on the utility's process.

payout_quote: Database of State Incentives for Renewables & Efficiency — Find Policies & Incentives Near You.
timing: Varies by utility program: instant point-of-sale discounts, or mail-in/online rebates typically paid 4-8 weeks after purchase and installation.
eligibility: Set by each utility/state program. Typical: must be a residential customer of the participating utility; equipment must meet the program's efficiency specs and be purchased within the program window; some rebates require pre-approval before purchase.
catches: This is a directory of thousands of separate programs, not one $1,000 offer — what you can get depends entirely on your utility and state.
Every rebate requires spending money on equipment or upgrades first; it is a discount, not cash earned.
Rebate amounts and qualifying product lists change yearly; always confirm the current program terms before buying.
Some utility rebates require pre-approval BEFORE purchase — buying first can disqualify you.
steps: Go to https://dsireusa.org and enter your 5-digit zip code to list incentive programs in your area.
Filter for residential rebate programs from your electric/gas utility and open the utility's program page for current amounts and terms.
Check whether the rebate needs pre-approval before purchase — if so, apply first.
Buy and install the qualifying efficient equipment within the program window and keep receipts.
Submit the utility's rebate application (online or mail-in) with proof of purchase; rebate arrives as a bill credit or check, typically in 4-8 weeks.
biggest_catch: This is a directory, not a single $1,000 offer — your actual rebate depends entirely on your utility, and every rebate requires spending money on equipment first; it is a discount, not cash earned.
notes: Verified the live DSIRE database 2026-09-22. DSIRE is the long-running DOE-supported national incentive database (operated by the N.C. Clean Energy Technology Center). PRODUCT NOTE: utility rebates are purchase discounts, not income — the honest app framing is 'save on upgrades you're already buying,' never earnings.
